newsitem.title: UK: National Power details overseas earnings.
newsitem.headline: National Power details overseas earnings.

text.p: National Power Plc said on Wednesday that overseas earnings were "now material and growing quickly" and said post-tax project income, before financing costs, from international investments was expected to rise to 145 million stg in 1997/98 from 70 million stg in 1996/97.

It said the net effect on profit after tax was expected to be 30 million stg in 1996/97 and 95 million stg the following year, with an annual contribution to earnings per share of 2.5 pence and 8.0 pence respectively.
At an investor relations conference in London Keith Henry, chief executive, said these overseas earnings would help underpin the company's financial objective of maintaining real growth in dividends.
He said National Power was confident of building on its international success and envisaged that in 2000 around 40 percent, some 2.0 billion stg, of its assets would be abroad.

On the domestic front, Henry said the end of special coal-backed contracts with the UK's regional electricity companies (RECs) in March 1998 and the opening of the supply market to full competition would provide the opportunity for new, lower-priced fuel purchase deals.
He said that in 1998 there would be a one-off change in the operating margin -- the difference between market-priced contracts and those in the five year coal-backed contracts with the RECs.
But the company did not expect prices to collapse in 1998 against current electricity contract prices.
Emerging competition in supply would impact on retail margins, not on generating margins, Henry said.
He said the entry of new players in the power generation market would be partly offset by the closure of older coal plant and Magnox nuclear plant.

The number of new entrants in prospect might also be exaggerated in the light of firmer gas prices, the inter-continental gas interconnector coming on stream in 1998, the end of back-to-back deals by the RECs and keener pool electricity prices.
National Power said that in the event of a future Labour government in the UK, changes in the regulatory regime were unlikely to have a direct impact on its business.
